title: 2. CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L11: Web Security 2 (XSS · CSRF · Files · SSRF · API · Proactive Controls): 2. CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery).

items: Browser auto-attaches cookies to every request to a domain, regardless of origin
Attacker tricks victim's browser (image tag, hidden form auto-submit, fetch) into hitting a state-changing endpoint
Bank server sees a valid session → executes the action

blocks.text: <!-- POST-based CSRF (auto-submitting form) --> <body onload="document.forms[0].submit()"> <form action="https://bank.com/transfer" method="POST"> <input name="to" value="evil"><input name="amount" value="50000"> </form> </body> ```

items: CSRF token (synchronizer) — random token per session, embedded in form, validated on POST/PUT/DELETE
Custom request header (X-Requested-With) — cross-origin requests cannot set custom headers without CORS preflight

blocks.text: Real-world: Gmail (2007) — CSRF on filter settings → attacker silently created an email-forwarding rule for the victim. Persistent access without ever stealing a password.
